text:
maya: fwd from customer - intermittent JSON parse failures in structured_output after we flipped them to redwood/llama-5b-v2 canary. Error: 'Unexpected token } in JSON at position 345' and it only happens for streaming responses.

sam: can you paste a raw chunk sequence and the exact API call? also which runtime + streaming mode (chunked vs sse)?

maya: pasted sanitized example from their logs below. it's the raw chunks as captured by their client (they concatenated bytes):
```
chunk1: {\"items\": [\"a\": 1, \"b\": 2
chunk2: },\"meta\": {\"id\":\"xyz\"}
```
client fails when merging -> looks like an extra closing brace appears in the middle of the stream.

oliver: interesting. that suggests either the model emitted an extra '}' token at a boundary or our streaming/chunking layer is inserting/duplicating a brace. @deploy-bot when was the canary for llama-5b-v2 pushed to this org?

deploy-bot: canary deploy redwood/llama-5b-v2 -> org:acme completed at 1723448000 by pipeline #deploy-427 :rocket:

jenna: i can try to reproduce. maya, can you get one of the failing request IDs? i want to replay with a dev key and capture raw TCP. try max_chunk_size=256 and stream=true for the replay.

oliver: repro steps I used locally:
1) curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer DEVKEY' -d '{\"prompt\":\"<long structured list>\", \"stream\": true, \"mode\": \"structured_output\" }' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
2) save raw bytes and concat them
I occasionally see a chunk boundary where a trailing '}' is followed by another '}' after concatenation, e.g. "...\"items\"]} } ,\"meta\":{...}" which breaks strict JSON consumers.

maya: customer reports it's most common with long arrays and their downstream webhook does strict JSON parse (no recovery). they estimate ~0.3% of streams fail since the canary.

sam: possible root causes to investigate: 1) model outputs a standalone '}' token when finishing a list 2) runtime chunking splits mid-UTF8/byte sequence and our reassembly inserts an extra delimiter 3) streaming proxy layer re-chunks and duplicates a boundary character when the last token of a chunk is a brace.

jenna: i checked proxy logs around the canary: we added a CRLF insertion for chunk delimiting in the new runtime path. i see cases where a chunk ending with '}' plus CRLF then next chunk starting with ',' gets normalized incorrectly -> duplication. sample log snippet:
```
...\"items\"]}\r\n,\"meta\":{...
```
That could result in an extra '}' after reassembly if trimming is off.

oliver: suggested mitigation plan:
- add strict pass-through mode for structured_output when stream=true for affected orgs (no proxy reformatting)
- add an automated regression test that concatenates chunk streams and verifies valid JSON output for typical templates
- monitor error rate and rollback canary if >0.1% failures over 30m

maya: customer priority = high, it's breaking their order ingestion webhooks. they requested either a hotfix or immediate rollback for their org.

sam: i'll spin up a P1 and attach the repro harness. will include curl + node client that concatenates raw bytes and runs JSON.parse to catch failure. @jenna can you pin acme canary traffic to 0 until we have a fix?

jenna: pinned acme to 0 at 1723459000 and enabled enhanced stream-boundary logging (request_id + chunk_index) for the next 2 hours. also added a short-lived feature-flag to force pass-through for structured_output for org:acme.

maya: i'll reply to the customer with ETA and ask for a few failing request_ids. thanks all.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll start the P1 doc and link traces/repro in the ticket.
